territorial_scope.description: Applies to the use of AI systems for real-time biometric identification by the Swedish Police Authority and Säkerhetspolisen.

evidence.quote: Lagen gäller för Polismyndighetens och Säkerhetspolisens

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Sets conditions under which the Swedish Police Authority and Säkerhetspolisen may use real-time facial or remote biometric identification AI systems in public places for law enforcement. Requires prior permission from a prosecutor or court, with urgent exceptions and notification duties; applies from a date set by government.
summary.long: The Act governs use by the Swedish Police Authority (Polismyndigheten) and Säkerhetspolisen of AI systems for real-time facial recognition or other real-time remote biometric identification in public places, where personal data processing falls under the Criminal Data Act (2018:1177). Use is allowed only when absolutely necessary to locate or identify a specified person in listed situations, including suspected trafficking, a missing person suspected of a crime, imminent risk of a serious crime endangering life or physical safety, and suspected crimes carrying four years' imprisonment or more; the benefit must outweigh the intrusion (5 §). Use requires prior permission: from a prosecutor for crime prevention and enforcement of sentences (6 §), and from a court on a prosecutor's application for investigation or prosecution (7 §). Permits state the person, purpose, time and area, last at most one month, and cover no more than absolutely necessary (10 §). Use may start without permission in urgent cases, with an application within 24 hours (13–14 §). Section 3 requires a fundamental-rights impact assessment under AI Act Article 27 and registration under Article 49 before first use; it exists in two versions tied to dates set by government. Identified persons must be notified, subject to secrecy exceptions (17–18 §). The Act contains no penalty provisions.

relations.target_text: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), cited for the definition of real-time remote biometric identification system, Articles 27 and 49, and Annex II
relations.note: Scope definition is by reference to Article 3.42 of the AI Act. Section 3 cites Art. 27 (fundamental rights impact assessment) and Art. 49 (registration). Section 4 cites Annex II offences.

relations.note: Defines the scope of the Act: it applies to processing of personal data covered by the Criminal Data Act.

relations.target_text: brottsbalken (Criminal Code), chapter 4, sections 1, 1 a and 1 b
relations.note: Offences of human trafficking, abduction and human exploitation are cited as conditions for use under section 4.

relations.target_text: rättegångsbalken (Code of Judicial Procedure), chapter 19 and chapter 27, section 28
relations.note: Section 7 names the court under chapter 19. Section 8 applies the Code's rules on coercive measures in criminal cases, except chapter 27, section 28 (public counsel).

notes: Section 3 appears twice: one version reads 'Upphör att gälla' (ceases to apply) and the other 'Träder i kraft' (enters into force), both tied to the day the government decides; the second adds registration under AI Act Art. 49 and allows use without registration when waiting is not possible. The text does not show which version is in force or the dates. 'Lag (2026:807).' follows the second version; its link to that version is inferred. The document's amendment note cites SFS 2026:807. Section 2 defines the scope by reference to the AI Act, so the Act's terms are needed to read it.

thresholds.measurement: Statutory penalty scale of the offence (imprisonment), as set out in the offence's penalty range
thresholds.consequence: Real-time facial recognition may be used to locate or identify a person reasonably suspected of an Annex II offence with a penalty scale of four years' imprisonment or more, to investigate or prosecute it.
thresholds.conditions: Use must be absolutely necessary; the person must reasonably be suspected of the offence (or of attempt, preparation or conspiracy to it); offence must be one referred to in Annex II to the AI Act.

thresholds.consequence: The period of an authorisation may not be set longer than absolutely necessary and may not exceed one month from the date of the decision.
thresholds.conditions: The period must not exceed what is absolutely necessary; the covered area(s) must not be larger than absolutely necessary.
